title: propagate-request-trace-to-tool-exec-and-tag-endpoint-metrics
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers observed gaps in observability when our OpenAI-compat API invoked external tool/function call handlers. Request-scoped IDs and tracing tags were not consistently propagated into the tool execution paths or the JSONL structured logs produced during streaming and function-call flows. That made postmortems and per-route cost/latency attribution difficult for function-heavy workloads.

What this PR does: Adds deterministic propagation of request_id and W3C traceparent baggage into the tool/executor boundary, and surfaces per-endpoint metric tags at the API gateway and runtime emitters. Specifically: 1) wire request_id + tracecontext through the OpenAI-compat adapter into ToolExecutor and FunctionCallRunner; 2) augment JSONL structured logging emitted during streaming and function calls with a minimal header that includes request_id, route, model_variant, and span_id; 3) add per-route metric tags (route_name, client_plan, auth_tier) to token and latency metrics so SLO dashboards can be filtered without additional correlation logic; 4) ensure streaming hop-by-hop headers don't drop tracecontext for long-lived SSE/WS streams by injecting periodic keepalive span checkpoints; 5) backward-compatible behavior: when no tracepresent, runtime generates traceparent and annotates logs accordingly.

Implementation notes: The change is implemented in three layers: adapter (openai_compat/adapter.go) which extracts/forwards incoming headers; runtime shim (runtime/trace/propagate.go) which normalizes traceparent and request_id and exposes a ContextCarrier interface; and tooling layer (tools/executor.go and tools/logging.go) which consumes ContextCarrier and attaches structured header JSON to streaming frames and function-call logs. We added a lightweight API in runtime ContextCarrier to avoid import cycles and kept the actual trace library usage behind a small wrapper so the tracing backend remains pluggable.

Compatibility & rollout: The feature is guarded by "obs.propagate_tool_trace" feature flag (default on for hosted). For Dedicated/Private we added a config toggle in console with a migration task note. Feature flag allows staged rollout for high-traffic customers. No API schema changes were made to OpenAI-compat endpoints.

Testing and QA: Unit tests for ContextCarrier behaviors and adapter header parsing added; integration test that runs a simulated tool invocation under streaming load and asserts that request_id appears in tool logs and in metric labels; e2e smoke test against legacy clients to ensure no impact when no tracepresent header exists. Load testing shows median latency increase of ~0.6ms on function-call hot path (within SLO).

Rollforward plan: Monitor new metric tags (per_route.trace_propagated.count and per_route.tool_call.latency.percentiles) in staging dashboards for 72h then enable for a small set of production routes. If errors spike, feature flag can be disabled per-cluster via Console.

Related: ENG-4321 (observability improvements for function-exec SLA), ENG-4389 (openai-compat streaming stability work), SUP-210 (customer support ticket citing opaque tool logs).
commits_summary:
3 commits:
- Normalize traceparent/request_id and add ContextCarrier wrapper (runtime)
- Propagate headers in openai_compat adapter and attach to streaming frames (adapter + streaming)
- Add structured JSON header emission in tools executor and tests (tools + logging)
diff_snippets: adapter.go: extract request-id and traceparent from headers and call runtime.Propagate(ctx, headers)
context_carrier.go: new interface ContextCarrier { GetRequestID() string; GetTraceParent() string } and helper constructors
executor.go: attach header json to tool stdout stream: \u003cheader\u003e{\"request_id\":...,\"route\":...}\u003c/header\u003e
review_comments: Arjun: Please confirm the behavior when incoming traceparent is malformed — do we generate a fresh trace or fail the request? (requested change)
Maya: We now validate traceparent and fall back to generating a new traceparent; added unit test to cover malformed-tracepath case.
Samantha: Can we avoid adding tags to the high-cardinality metric 'token_count' directly? Suggest tagging only aggregated metrics.
Maya: Updated metrics to tag only per-route aggregates (token_count_agg) rather than raw per-token counters; adjusted tagging in pkg/metrics/tags.go.
Leo: CI flake on streaming tests looked unrelated — reran and it passed.
merge_commit_message:
squash: propagate request/trace into tool execution and add per-route metric tags

Includes adapter, runtime shim, tools executor changes, and docs
release_notes: Add request_id and W3C trace propagation into tool/function call executions and streaming frames; emit per-route metric tags for aggregated token and latency metrics to improve observability and attribution (feature flag: obs.propagate_tool_trace).
notes_for_support: If customers report missing request_id in tool logs, check obs.propagate_tool_trace feature flag and ensure proxy preserves incoming traceparent header. For Private installs verify feature-gate config in deploy/k8s/feature-gate-config.yaml.
attention_items: Monitor per_route.tool_call.latency p95 for routes with heavy function-call traffic
Watch for metric cardinality increases if customers enable client_plan tagging in high-cardinality environments
changelog_entry: Observability: propagate request/trace to tool executions and add per-route metric tags (feature-flagged).
notes_for_dedicated_ops: Dedicated clusters: config toggle available via Console > Feature Flags. When enabling for a tenant, validate metric storage retention and cardinality.
